C-index 0.609 (95% bootstrap CI 0.599–0.618, 200 resamples) on 7,809 patients never trained on · log-rank χ² = 337 (2 df) · p = 7.5e-74
1,440 patients, 468 events; 93 candidate genes (of 341 covered for every patient, mutated in ≥30); elastic net, alpha 0.5, seed 1. The risk score is
OncoCast's 0–10 scale: 0 and 10 are the lowest and highest held-out score (raw linear predictor −0.315 to 1.06). 72 of the 93 candidate genes were never
kept, so are not on the volcano. Left out: 27 never held out (so unscored and in no group). 6 more genes were kept in at least one run; they are in the result,
not drawn. Validation: 7,809 of 7,809 patients of “NSCLC (MSK-CHORD)” scored; 0 on panels missing one of the model's 21 weighted genes, 0 with no panel
left out. Association, not cause: a gene's weight is its link to OS with the other candidates held fixed, in this cohort. Without strata, a gene that marks a cancer
type carries that type's prognosis; on a cohort of several cancer types, stratify by CANCER_TYPE. Each patient is scored only by models that did not train on
them. The group cuts are equal quantiles of the score, chosen without the outcome. Genes outside the panels every patient was sequenced on are not
candidates, so a patient is never counted as wild-type for a gene they were not tested for. The C-index ignores delayed entry. Seeded (seed 1): the same
document gives the same model. External validation on “NSCLC (MSK-CHORD)” (msk_chord_2024): each patient scored with the ensemble's mean
coefficients (every gene's coefficient averaged over all 10 runs, zero where a run dropped it) and cut at the training thresholds; 0 patients on panels missing
one of the model's 21 weighted genes are left out rather than scored as wild-type. Harrell's C-index (within strata) with a seeded bootstrap interval (200
resamples). The two studies' baselines, panels and vocabularies are not harmonized, and a patient enrolled in both under different identifiers cannot be
